candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes features highly characteristic of sparganosis: migratory discomfort, history of impure water consumption, tubular hypoechoic structures without blood flow on Doppler, multiple small fat-layer lesions, and a mobile lump in a patient from an endemic context. BIRADS 4a/4b are radiological assessment categories assigned during workup, not a final diagnosis. Breast cancer is a distinct and conflicting diagnostic entity; the imaging morphology (tubular, avascular, migratory, multi-focal fat-layer nodules) is inconsistent with primary breast malignancy and is instead characteristic of parasitic infestation (sparganosis).
candidate_relations.scope_detail: BIRADS 4a/4b are imaging risk categories, not a final diagnosis; breast cancer is a different diagnostic entity from sparganosis

case_quality_flags: Classic sparganosis presentation: tubular avascular hypoechoic lesion, migratory symptoms, impure water exposure history, multiple fat-layer nodules — reference diagnosis well-supported by clinical record
